population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: ever 32.0% − current 23.0% = 9.0% of adults used and are off now. The 5.5 pts of new ever-users since 2030 split into 4.5 on and 1.0 already off. Of the 26.5 pts who had used by 2030, 18.5 are on and 8.0 are off. On: 4.5 + 18.5 = 23.0. Off: 1.0 + 8.0 = 9.0. Within the 2030 cohort: 12.5 of the 18.8 then on stayed on (66% two-year persistence, up from ~50%; monthly MariTide, clinic-administered dosing and adherence-gated premiums explain the rise). 6.3 stopped and joined the 7.7 already off, making a pool of 14.0. 6.0 of those restarted (43% over two years, down from 55%, because the pool now holds more deliberate opt-outs). 12.5 + 6.0 = 18.5. Cycled: the 8.9 pts who had cycled by 2030, plus ~2.6 pts of first-time restarts, gives 11.5 of 32.0 ever-users = 36%. Adults ≈270M, so current users ≈62.1M. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%): 2.4 + 8.25 + 8.88 + 3.45 = 22.98 ≈ 23.0. 65+ users ≈ 0.15 × 0.23 × 270M ≈ 9.3M. Income thirds average (25 + 23.5 + 20.5)/3 = 23.0. Top-third use is flat at 25. Older affluent users stay on, often quietly and at lower doses, while affluent 18–39s taper off under the 'unmedicated' ideal. Bottom-third use rose from 13 to 20.5 through HRSA expansion, six Medicaid adherence waivers, cheaper cash prices and employer premium differentials. Off-drug: ~24.3M adults used and stopped, plus ~184M never used. The never-users now split three ways: people who could not get it, people who refused on principle, and affluent young adults for whom never having used is itself a status marker. Pediatric: 0.8% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 585k, flat overall. Adolescent (12–17) use rose. 6–11 use peaked at ~110k in mid-2031 and fell to ~60k after the November 2031 growth signal, as new starts collapsed and some families withdrew. The oldest adolescent cohorts have about 9 years of exposure.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge renewed (Dec 2031 omnibus) through 2033. Payment falls from $275 to $225/month under the negotiated step-down; the copay stays $50 and the DEXA/strength counselling visit for 65+ is kept. A new continuation criterion requires ≥5% weight loss at 6 months or a documented cardiometabolic, renal or apnea endpoint to renew. About 3.4M beneficiaries use the Bridge for obesity: 3.4M × $225 × 12 ≈ $9.2B/yr. Medicare overall pays 16% of fills ≈ 9.9M users (9.3M adults 65+ plus ~0.6M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays 12% ≈ 7.45M users at $225: 7.45M × $225 × 12 ≈ $20.1B/yr, federal and state combined. Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged. CMS approved four more (Ohio, Tennessee, Missouri, Georgia) on the same ≥80% PDC and weigh-in template, and these allow a logged clinic-administered monthly MariTide dose as an alternative compliance route. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program FY2032 appropriation is $5.6B: 3.0M generic liraglutide users × $75 contract × 12 = $2.70B, plus 1.4M semaglutide users (cessation, AUD, and gambling disorder since Jun 2032) × $165 × 12 = $2.77B, ≈ $5.47B. Nine states use sports-betting problem-gambling earmarks to fund free semaglutide for ~0.1M people: 0.1M × $165 × 12 ≈ $0.2B.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 80+ semaglutide brands at $6–40/month and launched generic tirzepatide in 2031 at $25–60. Generic semaglutide is sold in Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey, China and most of the EU's neighbourhood; generic oral semaglutide in ~180 countries. In the US, Paragraph IV settlements disclosed in 2031 set generic semaglutide entry for 2033, and tirzepatide remains protected beyond that.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~62.1M users: commercial 37% (23.0M), Medicare 16% (9.9M), Medicaid 12% (7.45M), public free provision 7.3% (4.5M: HRSA 4.4M + state gambling programmes 0.1M), cash/direct 13% (8.1M), gray 14.7% (9.1M) = 100%; 23.0 + 9.9 + 7.45 + 4.5 + 8.1 + 9.1 ≈ 62.1M. Managed decline (Jan 2031 CMS–manufacturer agreement, extended to TrumpRx and three large PBMs): semaglutide cash $349→$249, tirzepatide $449→$299, oral starting doses $199→$149, orforglipron $199, MariTide $299 (launched at that price). Wegovy list is still $1,349. Retatrutide list is still $1,499; allocation has eased but it has no cash-portal price and is reached through commercial plans or concierge cash. Employer coverage rose from 57% to 61%, and about two-thirds of covering employers now attach conditions: an outcome-based HIPAA wellness premium differential (up to 30%) tied to BMI or waist targets, or a verified-adherence requirement. Many satisfy the adherence requirement with monthly MariTide administered at onsite or partner clinics. Commercial pharmacy trend has slowed to ~+11%. Gray share fell from 18% to 14.7% as legal cash prices came down, but absolute gray users are flat at ~9M. Compounded 503A semaglutide sells for $99–199 and Indian mail pens for $6–40. 'Research' retatrutide vials still circulate at $100–200. 'Focus/calm' wellness subscriptions shrank to ~1.1M after FTC consent orders and now count inside cash.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Feb 2032)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide, approved Sep 2031)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029; growth-monitoring boxed requirement added Mar 2032)
gambling disorder, moderate-to-severe, adjunct to behavioural therapy (semaglutide, Jun 2032)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: compulsive shopping, pornography and 'screen' compulsion in adults, marketed by telehealth brands as 'compulsion care' after the gambling label
'metabolic health' longevity regimens with DEXA, now often low-dose and undisclosed among older affluent users
semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology, sharply reduced since the growth signal
sports-betting relapse prevention bundled by employers in the gaming industry itself
scheduled 'dose holidays' around weddings, holidays and tours, now discussed in prescribing guidance
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Next-gen driver (monthly) is realised by MariTide: BLA filed Jul 2030, approved Sep 2031 (≥12 months after filing), ~20% mean loss at 72 weeks, at a $1,199 list and $299 cash. It reached ~2.5M users by end 2032 under capacity limits. Its long half-life means dose holidays and side effects both last weeks. Amycretin was resubmitted Q2 2031 after Novo's facility reinspection and approved Feb 2032 (weekly), with limited launch supply. Survodutide's resubmission drew a major amendment, and its PDUFA date slipped to Q1 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 and are not on the market. No implant is on the US market. The compulsion driver is realised as a supplement: an NIH-co-funded and Novo-sponsored phase 3 in gambling disorder read out Mar 2031, the sNDA was filed Sep 2031 with priority review, and approval followed Jun 2032. Compulsive buying and sexual compulsion are not DSM disorders and remain off-label. The incretin market is ≈$142B in 2032: US volume rose ~24%, US net prices fell ~20%, and ex-US generic erosion deepened.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. With MariTide, first-dose vomiting is common and an episode cannot be reversed by skipping a dose for weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MariTide label requires titration via a lower initial dose; severe gastroparesis caution retained.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established; persistence after discontinuation is still disputed. MDL 3094 holds ~55,000 filed and tolled claims. The second bellwether (Jun 2031) went for the defence. Settlement talks are court-supervised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines a persistent-gastroparesis label. Reserves raised in 2031 filings; no global settlement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; absolute numbers rising with retatrutide, amycretin and research-peptide use.
No causal confirmation; low absolute risk. An Aug 2031 Daubert ruling excluded plaintiffs' general-causation experts, dismissing ~6,000 pancreatitis claims, now on appeal to the Third Circuit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; litigation track paused pending appeal.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Population problem in 65+, about 1.5× sarcopenia criteria after more than 2 years. Still most visible in low-efficacy, unmonitored, low-protein users, a group the HRSA expansion and new waivers enlarged.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label stands; Bridge counselling visit retained; HRSA and the new waivers still carry no body-composition requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term and cycling users, concentrated in women. The interim pediatric bone-accrual study (2031) shows lower-than-expected BMD Z-score gains in 6–11 starters, which could not be separated from weight-loss effects.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA recommended in 65+ and postmenopausal women; pediatric bone data folded into the Mar 2032 growth-monitoring label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Lilly's retatrutide postmarketing study (Oct 2031) found clinically meaningful anhedonia on the validated SHAPS scale in ~7% at the top dose versus ~3% at the lowest, dose-dependent and largely reversible within 8–12 weeks of stopping. Surveys put reduced pleasure at ~12–16% of long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Adverse Reactions section added for retatrutide (Feb 2032). FDA required class-wide postmarketing anhedonia studies. FTC consent orders (2031) with four 'focus/calm' brands bar mood claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Structural stops continue: the 2×90-day cessation cap, waiver lockouts, and now Bridge non-responder cut-offs at 6 months.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation ongoing; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D and protein insufficiency signals persist in older and low-income users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of adult follow-up and nine years in adolescents. The registry signal in 6–11s (below) is the first developmental finding.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; pediatric registry expanded to include semaglutide off-label use.

safety_ledger.effect: Pediatric growth deceleration and delayed pubertal onset (early starters)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Interim pediatric registry analysis (Nov 2031, ~38k children who started at ages 6–11): height velocity ~0.6 cm/yr below matched controls in the first two years, and thelarche delayed by a median ~7 months in girls. Weight loss, illness and socioeconomic confounding are not yet separated. No final-height data exist.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Nov 2031). Label update (Mar 2032) requires height, Tanner staging and growth-velocity checks every 6 months for 6–11. AAP guidance restricts 6–11 use to severe obesity with comorbidity. HRSA sites must document growth checks for children.

safety_ledger.effect: Restrictive eating / ARFID-pattern diagnoses in adolescents who started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Two claims-database studies (2032) find ~1.6× the expected rate of new restrictive-eating diagnoses among adolescents who started before 14, concentrated after discontinuation. Surveillance bias is likely.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change; FDA requested registry psychiatric endpoints.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls are flat at the 2030 level. Lower legal prices pulled some users back, but vial dosing errors and impure 'research' retatrutide persist.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning letters and import alerts continue; first DOJ indictment of a peptide distributor (2032); no prosecution of individual users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; more often reported in research-peptide users.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume losses in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks continue, at about two-thirds of the 2028–30 rate, as adoption growth slows and the base effect fades. Majors finish their indulgent-brand sales. A small premium 'full-plate' segment grows among affluent under-35s: butter, whole-milk dairy, heritage breads, marketed as 'unmedicated'. Protein and fibre formats grow but are saturating. Discount grocers in waiver states report weigh-in-week basket dips.

alcohol.state: AUD and cessation coverage keep cutting into heavy-drinker volume. Spirits volume is down again and beer is flat-to-down. A craft 'appetite' revival in cocktail bars in Austin, Brooklyn and Nashville is real and small. Tobacco declines continue to feed state excise shortfalls.

restaurants.state: Value-volume chains keep closing units. Austin's East Side is the visible case of the inversion: 'appetite rooms' and no-portion-limit barbecue and tasting counters court a tech crowd under 35 that eats loudly as a statement. Protein-forward fast casual is steady. Attach rates for alcohol remain lower than 2026.

apparel.state: Size runs stay wide. The 'athletic cut' is losing its premium, and a 'fed cut' with fuller seat and waist is the new boutique story. Plus-size retail stabilises at a smaller base.

fitness.state: Strength-and-DEXA studios still grow but more slowly. 'Natural' gyms and strength meets with drug-free attestation, including incretins, emerge as a premium niche. Low-cost gyms gain members through employer wellness differentials.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend slows to ~+11% as net prices fall. Gambling-disorder parity adds a fourth backdoor indication. Benefit design shifts from exclusion to conditioning: outcome-based premium differentials, adherence verification and monthly-dose clinic partnerships. Employer coverage rises to 61%.

pharma.state: Lilly remains the volume and margin leader. Amgen enters with MariTide and wins employer clinic contracts. Novo stabilises after the amycretin approval and the gambling label. Net price erosion is offset by volume, and the 2033 US semaglutide generic date hangs over Novo's guidance. Generic liraglutide makers' HRSA contracts grow, then wobble after the pediatric signal.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness has become cheap and now signals coverage, not money. Among affluent adults under 40, the scarce signal is visible appetite: eating a full plate in public, a body with some softness and real strength, and the claim of never having used or having tapered off. Older affluent users mostly stay on, at low doses, and stop talking about it.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The 'Charlotte build' still exists among bankers aged 40–55, but recruiters in Austin's tech sector now read it as dated, 'pharma-finished'. A thin body with little muscle reads as waiver or HRSA. A lean, fed, unmedicated body reads as old money or good genes, and that is the body people now covet and fake. Some top-third young adults buy 'off-ramp' taper programmes with a coach and DEXA to come off without regaining much.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals bifurcate. Medicated households keep small portions. Affluent young hosts throw 'full table' dinners where finishing your plate is a gesture. Families with a child on liraglutide now have a growth chart on the fridge next to the dosing calendar. Weddings still run two menus.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles have moved from naming the molecule to 'never-used' or 'tapered' badges, which some apps verify through pharmacy-history consent. 'Monthly' (MariTide) is read as employer- or waiver-managed. Mismatched appetites remain a standard couples-therapy topic.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has split in meaning. For the poor and the conditioned, untreated craving is still a liability that premiums and waivers price. For the affluent young, appetite is a luxury good and proof of an unmanaged self. The gambling label widened clinical appetite to include betting.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Validated retatrutide data (~7% clinically meaningful anhedonia at the top dose vs ~3% at the lowest) and the pediatric signal turned 'the grey' from a marketed feature into a common complaint. About 12–16% of long-term users report reduced pleasure. Roughly one long-term user in three reports at least one deliberate dose holiday in the past year. 'Focus' subscriptions shrank from 1.5–2M to ~1.1M after FTC consent orders, and most employers quietly dropped them as perks.
interior_life.framing: A side effect people manage. Clinicians say 'dose-dependent anhedonia' and now ask about it at refill. Users talk about 'grey weeks', 'coming up for air' and 'holiday math', the planning needed to skip a dose without falling under 80% PDC. Telehealth brands sell 'compulsion care' rather than calm.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Conditioning clashes with holidays. Weekly users can skip one dose a quarter and keep ≥80% PDC, so holidays cluster around performance reviews, pitches and family events. Employers that verify adherence with clinic-administered MariTide bypass the union contract language barring PBM data, and two of those three unions have filed grievances. Monthly users report being unable to take a holiday at all because of the half-life. Sales and creative staff still lower their dose before pitches.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' work is no longer a niche label, because nearly every touring musician now describes their dosing. The unmedicated circuit has become a genre with its own festivals. Sports-betting handle in New Jersey and Ohio is softer, operators blame the gambling label on earnings calls, and some sponsor 'responsible play' clinics. Leisure stays intense and short.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists routinely ask about dose and holiday timing. Couples coordinate holidays for anniversaries. MariTide users describe intimacy on a monthly cycle, flatter in the week after the shot. Partners of gambling-disorder patients describe relief and distance in the same sentence.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The fights are over conditioning, children and gambling money. Waiver plaintiffs and union lawyers attack adherence tracking. Parent groups in Ohio and Georgia attack free pediatric liraglutide after the growth signal. State treasurers note that problem-gambling funds now buy a drug that erodes the tax base they come from. 'Are you on?' has become 'Have you ever been?', and two 2032 congressional candidates campaigned as 'never-used'.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access on indications (gambling disorder, MariTide, amycretin), and more assertive on developmental and psychiatric safety: the pediatric Drug Safety Communication, the growth-monitoring label, class anhedonia postmarketing studies and FTC consent orders. Gray-market enforcement remains symbolic apart from one DOJ distributor indictment.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Subsidy expanded. The FY2032 omnibus raised HRSA to $5.6B (3.0M liraglutide users, 1.4M semaglutide users for cessation, AUD and gambling) and renewed the Medicare Bridge at $225/$50 through 2033. Nine states fund free semaglutide from sports-betting problem-gambling earmarks. There is still no mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning is now the dominant coverage design. Six Medicaid adherence waivers are in force (Indiana and Arkansas unchanged; Ohio, Tennessee, Missouri and Georgia approved 2031–32 on the same terms plus a clinic-administered monthly option). The Bridge adds a 6-month response criterion. About two-thirds of covering employers use outcome-based premium differentials or verified adherence. HRSA sites still require only refill pickup for adults; children now need documented growth checks.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT apnea clearance still makes tirzepatide a de facto requirement for some drivers. The Army's recruit policy stands, with a new exclusion for recruits who started incretins before 14 pending growth data. The VA added semaglutide for gambling disorder under its 2032 guideline update.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs remain. The managed price step-down was partly a trade for tariff relief on onshored fill-finish capacity. Amgen's MariTide capacity rations its launch. India's generic tirzepatide (2031) creates a new gray-market input, and the 2033 US semaglutide generic date shapes trade talks over Indian API.

events.event: CMS and the three incretin makers announce a negotiated step-down extended to TrumpRx and major PBMs: cash semaglutide falls to $249, tirzepatide to $299 and oral starting doses to $149; Medicare and Medicaid payment drops to $225 a month
FDA approves Amgen's MariTide, the first monthly incretin injection, at a $1,199 list and $299 cash price; large employers sign onsite-clinic administration contracts within weeks

Lilly's retatrutide postmarketing study reports dose-dependent clinically meaningful anhedonia in about 7% of top-dose users; FDA orders class-wide anhedonia studies and the FTC finalises consent orders with four 'focus' telehealth brands

Interim pediatric registry analysis finds slower height velocity and delayed puberty in children who started liraglutide at 6–11; FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication and new pediatric starts fall by more than half within three months

FY2032 omnibus raises the HRSA Community Incretin Access Program to $5.6B and renews the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2033 at $225, adding a six-month weight-response test for continued coverage; CMS approves four new Medicaid adherence waivers the same quarter

FDA approves semaglutide as an adjunct treatment for moderate-to-severe gambling disorder, bringing it under mental-health parity; nine states route sports-betting problem-gambling funds to free provision

open_tensions: Coverage is now conditional for the people least able to pay, through waivers, premium differentials and Bridge response tests, while affluent young adults turn away from the medicated body. Public money and payroll rules are holding the poor to a body standard the rich have started to abandon.

Monthly clinic-administered MariTide makes adherence observable without PBM data, bypassing union contract protections and removing the dose holiday that users say keeps the grey bearable. Grievances and the Indiana disability challenge are unresolved.

The pediatric growth signal sits against free generic liraglutide at FQHCs and roughly 60k children still on drug. Final-height and pubertal-outcome data are years away, and parent groups and pediatric endocrinologists are pulling in opposite directions.
States now spend sports-betting tax revenue on a drug that shrinks that revenue, while the 2033 US semaglutide generic date threatens to collapse prices and gray-market economics in the next window.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; generic_us remains false.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still covers semaglutide for smoking cessation as two 90-day courses a year, and benefits managers still call AUDIT-score drift 'indication shopping'.

prose.headline: Thin Got Cheap. Now the Rich Are Buying Back Their Appetite, and Your Employer Is Counting Your Shots
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2032 nearly one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, about sixty-two million people. The price fell, but it did not collapse. In January 2031 Washington and the drugmakers agreed on a step-down: semaglutide at $249 a month through the cash portal, tirzepatide at $299 and the starter pill at $149. Medicare and Medicaid now pay $225. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349, and retatrutide still lists at $1,499 and has no cash-portal price. Paragraph IV settlements set generic semaglutide for 2033, and that date hangs over every forecast.

The bigger change is in how coverage works. Insurers used to exclude the drugs. Now they set conditions. Six states run Medicaid programmes in which coverage depends on refills and weigh-ins. Indiana and Arkansas run theirs exactly as before, and Ohio, Tennessee, Missouri and Georgia have copied the template. The Medicare Bridge was renewed through 2033, but beneficiaries who have not lost five percent by six months lose it. About two-thirds of employers that cover the drugs now tie premiums to a waist measurement or a verified dose. Amgen's MariTide, approved in September 2031, made the verified dose easy. It is a single monthly shot given at the workplace clinic and logged there. It needs no pharmacy data, so the union contracts that bar employers from seeing PBM records do not reach it.

The free programme grew alongside the conditions. The federal community-health-centre programme now has $5.6 billion and about four and a half million users. Most get generic liraglutide. The rest get semaglutide to quit smoking, drink less or, since June, gamble less. That last approval came under mental-health parity, as the alcohol one did. Nine states now pay for the drug out of the sports-betting taxes earmarked for problem gambling, and the betting companies say on earnings calls that it is cutting into their business.

The drug also showed up in children's growth records. In November 2031 the paediatric registry required by the 2029 label reported that children who started liraglutide between six and eleven were growing about six-tenths of a centimetre a year more slowly than matched peers, and that girls were entering puberty around seven months later. No one can yet separate the effect of the drug from the effect of the weight loss, and no final heights exist. New starts in that age group halved. About sixty thousand children remain on the drug, measured every six months. A separate claims study has found more restrictive eating among teenagers who started young. Nobody yet knows whether that means anything.

The quiet that wellness brands sold in 2030 is now a complaint. Lilly's own data found real anhedonia in about seven percent of top-dose retatrutide users. The FTC ended the 'focus' marketing, and most employers dropped those subscriptions as a perk. Users plan dose holidays around weddings and reviews. Skipping one weekly shot a quarter keeps them above eighty percent adherence. Monthly users cannot skip at all.

What a thin body means has flipped. Thin now reads as covered, a sign of the waiver, the clinic or the premium discount. In Austin's East Side, tech workers under thirty-five crowd into barbecue counters and full-table dinners, and they eat in public as a statement. Dating apps verify 'never-used' badges. Tailors cut for a fuller waist. The bankers in Charlotte still have the retatrutide build, but younger people call it pharma-finished, and the older affluent users who stayed on have mostly stopped talking about it. Snack volumes keep falling, more slowly. Spirits keep falling. Lilly, Novo and Amgen report record volume at lower prices.

The country is leaner and calmer, and more of it is measured. The people being measured are mostly not the ones who decided that thin no longer counted for much.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rosa Delgado parks at the distribution centre outside Columbus at 5:40 and goes to the clinic trailer before her shift. It is the third Tuesday. The nurse scans her badge, swabs her belly and logs the MariTide. The app on her phone turns green. That green keeps her family premium $212 a month lower.

She had wanted to skip this one. Her sister's quinceañera party is Saturday, and Rosa wanted to taste the mole the way she used to. But the shot lasts a month, and a missed log costs the discount for the whole quarter. She looks at the green and goes in.

At lunch she eats half a turkey wrap and gives the rest to Darnell, who is off Wegovy and proud of it. He says his wife likes him better hungry.

At three she leaves early for the health centre on Parsons Avenue. Mateo is ten and has been on the free liraglutide pen since he was eight. A nurse in a cartoon-print smock stands him against the wall, then has him lie down and checks him a second way. She types for a long time.

"He's still on his curve," she says. "Lower part of it."

Rosa asks whether she should stop the pen.

"That's a conversation with Dr. Hsu. Next visit's in six months."

In the car Mateo asks if he can have fries. She says yes, large. He looks at her as if it's a trick.

At home she pencils a mark on the doorframe above last spring's, a little higher. She stands there with the pencil and doesn't feel much. She can't tell if that's the shot.
